newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Exiles say Iran executes 22 people in March.
newsitem.headline: Exiles say Iran executes 22 people in March.

text.p: An Iranian exile group said on Monday at least 22 people had been officially reported executed in Iran this month in what it described as a drive to head off popular uprisings.

"Fearing popular uprisings, the mullah's anti-human regime has resorted to mnore public executions to create an atmosphere of intimidation and terror in society at large," the Paris-based National Council of Resistance said in a statement.

The statement, released in Geneva and sent to the current session of the United Nations Human Rights Commission, said two people were hanged in the main square of the city of Sedeh and two others in Shahin-Shah on March 12.
All four were flogged before being hung, said the council, which is linked to the Iraq-based Mujahideen Khalq armed Iranian opposition group. It did not say what the charges against them were.
The statement said four people were hanged in Tehran's Qasr prison on March 12 for "moral offences" and two others were executed at the prison in Mashad, northeast Iran.
It also said 12 people whose executions were publicly announced in the first week of the month were hanged in Khorassan and Azerbaijan provinces. It did not say what they were accused of.
The statement was issued as the U.N. commission moved into the second week of its annual month-and-a-half long session in Geneva. It is expected to hear a report on the rights situation in Iran.

The exile group said it wanted to draw attention to "the persistent crimes" of the Iranian government and it called on the international community "to take urgent measures for an oil and a trade embargo against this medieval dictatorship."
